exposure: residence in rural and remote areas
cohort: 2171 mothers and 2438 babies retrieved by aeromedical transport for pregnancy-related issues
finding: Pregnant women retrieved by aeromedical transport had higher rates of preterm birth, cesarean section, low birth weight, neonatal resuscitation, special care nursery admission, and stillbirth compared to the general Australian pregnant population.
mod_finding: Over one-third of transferred women gave birth by Caesarean section (n = 812; 37.4%).
